title: How to Construct Domain Specific LLM Evaluation Systems: Hamel Husain and Emil Sedgh
talk_summary: Hamel Husain and Emil Sedgh describe how Rechat built a domain-specific eval system for their real-estate AI agent: start with cheap deterministic assertions/unit tests derived from observed failure modes, log traces, and build a low-friction internal data-viewing/labeling app for human review, only later adding LLM-as-judge aligned to human labels. They report that this framework let them rapidly raise success rates and made fine-tuning feasible for cases few-shot prompting couldn't solve.

takeaways.technique: Assertion-first eval layer before LLM judges
takeaways.what_they_do: Write many simple deterministic unit tests/assertions for observed failure modes (emails not sent, invalid placeholders, repeated details) and run them in CI, logging results to an existing BI tool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to try to write down as many assertions and unit tests as you can about the failure modes

takeaways.technique: Low-friction internal trace viewer + labeling app
takeaways.what_they_do: Build a small custom Gradio/Streamlit app that surfaces domain-specific trace metadata and doubles as a human-labeling tool, because off-the-shelf tools had too much friction.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's absolutely critical if you have any friction in looking at data people are not going to do it

takeaways.technique: Align LLM judge to human labels via spreadsheet
takeaways.what_they_do: Have a domain expert label critique data in a spreadsheet and iterate the LLM judge prompt until it agrees with the human, before trusting it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: keep iterating on that until my LM as a judge is in alignment with my human judge

takeaways.technique: Synthetic inputs to bootstrap test cases
takeaways.what_they_do: Use an LLM to role-play the end user and generate diverse inputs/scenarios to get test coverage before real users exist.
takeaways.evidence_quote: using llms to synthetically generate inputs is a good way to bootstrap these test cases

takeaways.technique: Use existing tools first, avoid tool-first thinking
takeaways.what_they_do: Log assertion results to tools already in use (Metabase) and defer buying eval platforms until the process is understood.
takeaways.evidence_quote: don't buy stuff use what you have when you when you're beginning

takeaways.technique: Fine-tune only after eval framework exposes hard cases
takeaways.what_they_do: Use the eval framework to curate good/failed cases for fine-tuning when few-shot prompting fails on structured+unstructured output and multi-tool commands.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we never managed to get everything that we wanted by F shot prompting
